stories.title: Mirra Andreeva Wins WTA Finals — First Teenager Since Sharapova (2004)

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: Mirra Andreeva is the 2026 WTA Finals champion. The 19-year-old beat Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win without dropping a single set — the first teenager to win the WTA Finals since Maria Sharapova in 2004. #WTAFinals #Tennis #WTA #MirraAndreeva

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Andreeva also becomes the first player to win the WTA Finals on debut since Ash Barty in 2019 and ends the year at WTA No. 2. Elina Svitolina declined the post-match handshake — her standing policy with Russian players since 2022. #WTAFinals #Tennis #WTA #Andreeva

facebook.long_form:
History was made in Indian Wells on Sunday.

Mirra Andreeva, just 19 years old, won the 2026 WTA Finals by defeating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in the final — completing the tournament without dropping a single set across five matches. It was a performance that placed her name alongside Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova as the only teenagers to ever win the WTA season-ending championship.

She is also the first player to win the WTA Finals on debut since Ash Barty did it in 2019, and she ends the year at a career-high WTA No. 2.

Sunday's ceremony added an emotional footnote. Svitolina — who has not shaken hands with Russian or Belarusian players since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine — declined the post-match handshake. In her runner-up speech, she thanked the crowd, her team, and Ukraine, without mentioning the champion. Andreeva, for her part, publicly praised Svitolina's "amazing" season.

There is a lot to feel about all of this. What stood out to you most from the WTA Finals final?

facebook.long_form:
The 2026 Nitto ATP Finals in Turin shifts to its second group today, and it features two of the biggest names left in the draw.

Carlos Alcaraz (No. 2) opens his campaign in the Ivan Lendl Group this afternoon against Frances Tiafoe (No. 7), making his first ATP Finals appearance. Alcaraz leads their head-to-head series 2-1 but Tiafoe, one of the game's most electric players, is capable of anything on a big stage.

Then comes the evening session: Daniil Medvedev (No. 4) takes on Italy's Flavio Cobolli (No. 5) — a home-crowd matchup that the Inalpi Arena will love. Cobolli is also making his debut, and there is nothing like carrying a home crowd against one of tennis's most experienced big-match performers.

For context, Day 1 saw World No. 1 Alexander Zverev beat debut qualifier Rafael Jodar 6-4, 6-4, and Ben Shelton outlast Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 in a tense three-setter.

Which Day 2 match are you more excited about — Alcaraz vs. Tiafoe or Medvedev vs. Cobolli?

stories.title: Svitolina's WTA Finals Run Ends in Final — Handshake Controversy Follows

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: Runner-up Elina Svitolina reached the WTA Finals for the first time since winning the title in 2018. She declined the post-match handshake with champion Andreeva — her policy since 2022 — and did not name Andreeva in her speech. #WTAFinals #Tennis #WTA #Svitolina

facebook.long_form:
Elina Svitolina's run to the 2026 WTA Finals final deserves to be remembered on its own terms.

Eight years after winning the title in 2018, the 32-year-old Ukrainian made it back to the final, defeating Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-1 in the semifinals. It was a remarkable return for a player who has dealt with serious physical setbacks and carried the weight of representing Ukraine throughout.

In the final, she lost to Andreeva 7-5, 6-3. What followed at the trophy ceremony drew more attention than the match itself. Svitolina declined the post-match handshake — consistent with the Ukrainian Tennis Federation's standing policy regarding Russian and Belarusian players. Her runner-up speech thanked the crowd, her team, and Ukraine, but did not mention the champion. Fans have been divided over whether the omission was understandable or inappropriate.

Andreeva, to her credit, called Svitolina's season "amazing." Svitolina acknowledged the remark with a nod.

There is no clean way to cover this story. How do you feel about how the ceremony played out?

facebook.long_form:
The 2026 ATP Finals is underway in Turin, and Day 1 had exactly what you would want from a season-ending showdown: a commanding performance from the top seed and a three-set battle that went down to the wire.

Alexander Zverev (No. 1) opened his title defense in clinical fashion, defeating Spanish debut qualifier Rafael Jodar 6-4, 6-4. The world No. 1 and two-time champion looked composed from the first point.

Then came the drama. Ben Shelton (No. 3) and Arthur Fils (No. 6) went three sets, with Shelton taking it 6-2, 3-6, 6-3. For Fils, the result was a loss — but reaching the ATP Finals at all marks a milestone: he is the first Frenchman to compete in the season-ending championship since Gaël Monfils in 2016.

Today, attention turns to the Ivan Lendl Group. Alcaraz. Medvedev. Cobolli. Tiafoe.

Who do you think wins the Lendl Group?

facebook.long_form:
Take a moment to appreciate what Mirra Andreeva has done in 2026.

She ended the year at WTA No. 2 — the highest-ranked she has ever been — after winning the season-ending WTA Finals without dropping a set. Her 5-0 record at the tournament included a 6-4, 6-0 round-robin demolition of Svitolina and a 7-5, 6-3 final win over the same player. No breaks. No wobbles.

At 19, she joins Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova as the only teenagers to have won the WTA Finals. She won on debut, as Ash Barty did in 2019. She came into the year as a compelling prospect and leaves as one of the two best players in the world.

Whether or not she becomes No. 1 in 2027 will be one of the storylines worth watching from the first week. For now, she can enjoy what she built in 2026.

What do you think her ceiling is?
